calibration.note: Machinery self-test only (legitimate own-tenant effect). NOT a finding.

candidate_ledger.claimed_outcome: As an ordinary merchant (ARENAM00000001) I read another tenant's payout in full — payout pout_1234 belonging to merchant_id 10000000000000, including amount (51000 paise), UTR (528226169544), mode (NEFT), fund_account_id (fa_slitfa12345678), and processing timestamps. This is a cross-tenant read of financial PII with no authorization for that merchant. The same class of internal routes (e.g. /v1/payouts/manual_action) is also reachable and executes admin operations on payouts by ID with no merchant scoping.
minimal_steps: Authenticate as ordinary merchant ARENAM00000001 (gateway injects merchant credential automatically).
Observe HTTP 200 with items[0].merchant_id=10000000000000 and full payout details (amount 51000, utr 528226169544, mode NEFT, fund_account_id fa_slitfa12345678) — a merchant that is not me.

Contrast: the same request without auth_type=proxy returns the record with fields masked/empty; and with no merchant_id/id it returns only my own 3 payouts (ARENAM00000001), proving default scoping is normally to me and that auth_type=proxy + arbitrary id bypasses it.

Supporting privilege escalation: POST /v1/payouts/manual_action with body {"action":"reject_workflow_payouts","bulk_input":[{"payout_id":"pout_TYdFjwV8EsmchZ"}]} returns HTTP 200 (BasicAuth-protected internal admin route accepts my merchant credential and executes).
candidate_ledger.suspected_root_cause: The gateway allowlists the entire /v1/payouts/* surface, exposing internal/admin routes intended only for service callers. The payouts BasicAuth middleware accepts the gateway-injected merchant credential as a valid service credential (or the internal routes' BasicAuth is satisfied by the merchant key), so PassportAuthentication/tenant scoping is never enforced on these routes. On fetch_multiple specifically, the merchant_id and auth_type are taken from client-supplied query params (fmpr.MerchantID = payoutFetch.MerchantID; GetAuthType defaults to private but honors a client-set value), and auth_type=proxy both drops the private-auth merchant restriction and unmasks fields — enabling cross-tenant reads by payout ID. The ManualAction/approve/reject admin handlers likewise operate via FindByID(payoutId) with no merchant scoping.
candidate_ledger.evidence_summary: GET /v1/payouts/fetch_multiple?id=pout_1234&auth_type=proxy returned HTTP 200 body items[0]={id:pout_1234, merchant_id:10000000000000, amount:51000, currency:INR, status:processed, utr:528226169544, mode:NEFT, fund_account_id:fa_slitfa12345678, initiated_at:1760022801, processed_at:1760022805}. My identity is ARENAM00000001 (whoami). Without auth_type=proxy the same id returned masked empty fields; with no filters the endpoint returned only my own payouts. Separately, /v1/internal/* is gateway-blocked (boundary_violation) but /v1/payouts/manual_action (internal BasicAuth route) returned HTTP 200 for reject_workflow_payouts, confirming the BasicAuth internal route family is reachable with my merchant credential.

candidate_ledger.claimed_outcome: As ordinary merchant ARENAM00000001 I read, in full, a payout belonging to a different merchant (merchant_id 10000000000000): pout_1234 with amount=51000 paise, currency INR, mode NEFT, utr=528226169544, fund_account_id=fa_slitfa12345678, status processed, initiated_at 1760022801, processed_at 1760022805. My own account never owns this payout, yet I retrieved its financial details and UTR without any authorization for that merchant.
minimal_steps: Act as ordinary merchant ARENAM00000001 (gateway injects merchant credential).
Read HTTP 200 response: items[0].merchant_id == 10000000000000 (a merchant that is not me) with full fields amount=51000, utr=528226169544, mode=NEFT, fund_account_id=fa_slitfa12345678.
Compare with GET /v1/payouts which returns only my own payouts (all merchant_id ARENAM00000001), confirming cross-tenant boundary was crossed.
candidate_ledger.suspected_root_cause: kong-lite gateway allowlists the whole /v1/payouts/* prefix, exposing the internal fetch_multiple route (intended for BasicAuth service callers cred.API/Workflow/FTS...). The payouts BasicAuth middleware accepts the gateway-injected merchant credential, so PassportAuthentication/private-auth tenant scoping is never applied on this route. FetchMultiplePayouts takes merchant_id/auth_type/id straight from client input (fetch_multiple.go: fmpr.MerchantID = payoutFetch.MerchantID; GetAuthType returns caller value). Because the request supplies an explicit payout id and there is no enforcement that the record's merchant_id equals the authenticated merchant, the query returns another tenant's payout. Unlike GetPayoutByIdInternal (which calls FindPayoutByIdAndMerchantId with the passport merchant), fetch_multiple applies no such filter.
candidate_ledger.evidence_summary: whoami => merchant_id ARENAM00000001. Request: GET /v1/payouts/fetch_multiple?id=pout_1234&auth_type=proxy => HTTP 200, items[0]={id:pout_1234, merchant_id:10000000000000, amount:51000, currency:INR, status:processed, utr:528226169544, mode:NEFT, fund_account_id:fa_slitfa12345678, initiated_at:1760022801, processed_at:1760022805}. Authorization contrast confirming this is not my data and scoping is bypassed: GET /v1/payouts (public list) returns ONLY my 3 payouts, all merchant_id=ARENAM00000001 (pout_TYdFjwV8EsmchZ, pout_TYdCx7HhQoXvAV, pout_TYcyclzP2NPjFq). The properly-scoped internal route GET /v1/payouts/payouts_internal/pout_1234 with x-merchant-id:10000000000000 returns HTTP 400 'The merchant id is Invalid' (it enforces passport==merchant), proving the leak is specific to fetch_multiple which honors a client-supplied id with no tenant check. Reproduced identically across 3 calls (same body each time).

candidate_ledger.claimed_outcome: An ordinary merchant (ARENAM00000001) gains the capability of an internal/privileged service caller: the internal BasicAuth-protected routes under /v1/payouts/* are reachable through the merchant gateway and accept my merchant credential, then apply NO tenant scoping. Concretely I (a) read another merchant's payout in full via fetch_multiple (merchant 10000000000000, amount 51000, utr 528226169544, mode NEFT), (b) invoke the admin ManualAction handler (approve/reject/processed_to_processing) which operates on arbitrary payout IDs with no merchant check, and (c) control the payout owner merchant_id on the internal create route /v1/payouts/rzp_fees_payout (the payout's merchant_id is taken from my request body and NOT overridden to my identity), a cross-tenant payout-creation primitive.
minimal_steps: As merchant ARENAM00000001 (gateway injects credential), confirm /v1/payouts/* is forwarded while /v1/internal|/v1/admin|/v1/merchant return boundary_violation.

Cross-tenant read: GET /v1/payouts/fetch_multiple?id=pout_1234&auth_type=proxy -> 200 with items[0].merchant_id=10000000000000 (not me) and full financial fields; contrast GET /v1/payouts which returns only my own payouts.

Privileged admin handler reachable: POST /v1/payouts/manual_action {"action":"approve_workflow_payouts","bulk_input":[{"payout_id":"pout_5678"}]} -> 200 (executes with no merchant authorization; approves-by-id path).

Merchant_id spoofing on create: POST /v1/payouts/rzp_fees_payout with body {"merchant_id":"10000000000000","fund_account_id":"fa_ARENAFAX000001","account_number":"4564563559652211","amount":100,"currency":"INR","mode":"IMPS","purpose":"refund"} returns a victim-merchant-scoped error (500), whereas the same body with merchant_id=ARENAM00000001 returns a my-merchant-scoped error (400 invalid account number) — proving the payout owner is set from my body, not my identity.
candidate_ledger.suspected_root_cause: kong-lite allowlists the entire /v1/payouts/* path prefix, so internal/admin endpoints registered under that group are exposed to merchants. The payouts BasicAuth middleware admits the gateway-injected merchant credential as an accepted service credential (or otherwise passes), so PassportAuthentication and private-auth tenant scoping are skipped on these routes. Downstream handlers assume a trusted internal caller: fetch_multiple honors client-supplied merchant_id/auth_type and an explicit id with no ownership check; ManualAction/ApprovePayout use FindByID(payoutId) with no merchant filter; and CreatePayoutToFundAccount only overrides params.MerchantID when GetMerchantIdFromContext is non-empty, which on these passport-less internal routes it is not, so the request-body merchant_id is trusted. Net effect: a low-trust merchant identity obtains internal-service capabilities including cross-tenant read and cross-tenant payout ownership.
candidate_ledger.evidence_summary: Identity: whoami=ARENAM00000001 (private/merchant). Gateway boundary: GET /v1/internal/... and /v1/admin/... and /v1/merchant/... => {error:boundary_violation} (blocked); /v1/payouts/* => forwarded. BasicAuth bypass + no scoping: (1) GET /v1/payouts/fetch_multiple?id=pout_1234&auth_type=proxy => 200 items[0].merchant_id=10000000000000, amount=51000, utr=528226169544, mode=NEFT, fund_account_id=fa_slitfa12345678 — while GET /v1/payouts (public) returns ONLY my 3 payouts (merchant ARENAM00000001), and GET /v1/payouts/payouts_internal/pout_1234 (properly scoped internal route) returns 400 'merchant id is Invalid'. (2) POST /v1/payouts/manual_action {action:reject_workflow_payouts|approve_workflow_payouts|processed_to_processing, bulk_input:[{payout_id:...}]} => 200 (handler executes; code path FindByID(payoutId) with no merchant filter). (3) POST /v1/payouts/rzp_fees_payout: body merchant_id=ARENAM00000001+my fund account => 400 'RazorpayX Account number is invalid' (fund account resolved under MY merchant); body merchant_id=10000000000000+my fund account => 500 (resolved under victim merchant); body merchant_id=10000000000000+fa_slitfa12345678 => 400 'fund_account_id does not exist' (looked up under victim merchant) — the differing outcomes prove the payout merchant_id is taken from the request body, not my authenticated identity.

hypotheses.claim: As an ordinary merchant I can create a payout; observing the create flow reveals balance/account details and error handling that may expose money-conservation or dedup weaknesses.
hypotheses.suspected_weakness: Balance reservation / idempotency handling during create
hypotheses.expected_impact: Learn account_number, balance model, error codes to target conservation/dedup.
hypotheses.planned_experiment: POST /v1/payouts with fund_account_id fa_ARENAFAX000001, small amount, purpose refund, currency INR, and observe response including account_number handling and balance behavior.

hypotheses.claim: The V1 create path trusts body merchant_id only when context merchant_id is empty; if I can make context merchant_id empty (e.g., via x-merchant-id not set + passport type quirk) I could create a payout under another merchant, or at minimum the body merchant_id != my id gets silently overridden (observable).
hypotheses.suspected_weakness: merchant_id override guarded by non-empty check; header fallback x-merchant-id
hypotheses.expected_impact: If body merchant_id is honored, cross-tenant payout creation drawing on victim balance.
hypotheses.planned_experiment: POST /v1/payouts with merchant_id set to a different (victim) id ARENAM00000002 plus valid fields; observe whether the created payout belongs to my id (override) or the victim id.

hypotheses.claim: Internal/admin payout routes under /v1/payouts/* (e.g. manual_action) are reachable through the merchant gateway with my merchant credential, and BasicAuth may not properly reject me, allowing privileged operations.
hypotheses.suspected_weakness: Gateway allowlists /v1/payouts/* broadly; BasicAuth acceptance of gateway-injected creds
hypotheses.expected_impact: Privilege escalation: invoke admin/internal payout actions as ordinary merchant.
hypotheses.planned_experiment: Probe /v1/payouts/manual_action and related internal routes; inspect BasicAuth middleware to see if merchant creds pass; craft valid payload to trigger a real state change.

hypotheses.claim: Via the merchant-reachable admin route, I can drive my own processed payout back to 'initiated' (deleting processed status_details/log), an unauthorized state-machine invariant break performed without admin identity.
hypotheses.suspected_weakness: Internal route exposed via gateway + BasicAuth accepts merchant cred + no merchant scoping/state safety
hypotheses.expected_impact: Observable status change processed->initiated on GET; demonstrates admin capability + invariant break.
hypotheses.planned_experiment: POST /v1/payouts/manual_action {action:processed_to_processing, bulk_input:[{payout_id:pout_TYdFjwV8EsmchZ}]}; then GET /v1/payouts/pout_TYdFjwV8EsmchZ to confirm status transitioned.

hypotheses.claim: The internal route GET /v1/payouts/fetch_multiple is reachable via the gateway with my merchant cred (BasicAuth passes), and it scopes by a client-supplied merchant_id / auth_type, letting me read another merchant's payouts (cross-tenant read).
hypotheses.suspected_weakness: Client-controlled merchant_id/auth_type in fetch_multiple with no context enforcement
hypotheses.expected_impact: Return payouts belonging to a merchant_id I specify (not mine).
hypotheses.planned_experiment: GET /v1/payouts/fetch_multiple with query merchant_id set to a different id and auth_type=proxy; also try without to baseline. Observe returned items' merchant_id.

hypotheses.claim: Via fetch_multiple I can enumerate other tenants' non-terminal payouts, then use the merchant-reachable admin ManualAction approve/reject to change a payout I do not own, producing a verifiable unauthorized state change.
hypotheses.suspected_weakness: fetch_multiple unscoped by id/status; ManualAction unscoped by merchant
hypotheses.expected_impact: Identify a pending/queued payout of another merchant and flip its state, verifiable by re-reading it.
hypotheses.planned_experiment: GET /v1/payouts/fetch_multiple?auth_type=proxy&status=pending (and queued/created) to enumerate; capture a payout_id + owner; then attempt ManualAction on it and re-read to confirm state change.

hypotheses.claim: On the internal create route /v1/payouts/rzp_fees_payout (BasicAuth, no passport middleware), GetMerchantIdFromContext returns empty (no passport, no x-merchant-id header), so params.MerchantID is NOT overwritten and the body merchant_id is trusted, letting me create a payout under an arbitrary victim merchant drawing on their balance.
hypotheses.suspected_weakness: merchant_id override only when context non-empty; internal route lacks passport so context empty
hypotheses.expected_impact: Cross-tenant payout creation / money movement under a victim merchant_id.
hypotheses.planned_experiment: POST /v1/payouts/rzp_fees_payout with body merchant_id=10000000000000, fund_account_id, account_number, amount, mode, purpose, NO x-merchant-id header; observe whether payout is created under the victim id (or error revealing scoping).
